pages.title: What you will learn
pages.body:
🎯 **By the end of this lesson you will be able to:**
- Explain the interrelationship of science, technology and innovation.
- Discuss technological advancements in the world and their impact on the Ghanaian environment.

pages.title: Defining Science, Technology and Innovation
pages.body: Science, technology and innovation are three closely related but distinct ideas that together shape how societies develop and solve problems. Science is the systematic study of the natural world through observation and experimentation, aimed at understanding how things work. Technology is the practical application of scientific knowledge to create tools, devices or systems that solve real problems. Innovation is the process of developing new ideas, methods or products, often by creatively applying science and technology in new ways.

lessons.subject: sci
lessons.title: How Science, Technology, Innovation and Society Connect

pages.title: How Science, Technology, Innovation and Society Connect
pages.body:
Scientific discovery, technological application, societal need, and environmental impact are four interconnected elements that influence one another continuously, rather than functioning in a simple, one directional chain.

- Science often begins with curiosity or a societal need, such as understanding why crops fail, which leads to new scientific knowledge, such as understanding soil nutrients.

- Technology takes this scientific knowledge and turns it into practical tools, such as improved fertilisers or irrigation systems.

- Innovation may then combine or adapt these technologies in creative new ways, such as designing low cost irrigation systems suited to smallholder farms.

- Society adopts, adapts, or sometimes resists these innovations depending on cost, culture, and perceived benefit, while the environment is affected, positively or negatively, by how these technologies are used.

pages.title: Technological Advancements and Their Impact on Ghana
pages.body:
Mobile phones, improved farming equipment, solar power, medical technology, and motor vehicles are examples of technological advancements that have had a significant impact, both positive and negative, on the Ghanaian environment and society, as summarised in the table below.

| **TECHNOLOGICAL ADVANCEMENT** | **IMPACT ON THE GHANAIAN ENVIRONMENT AND SOCIETY** |
|---|---|
| **Mobile phones and the internet** | Improved communication and access to information, but increased demand for electricity and electronic waste |
| **Improved farming equipment and methods** | Increased crop yields and food security, but sometimes increased fuel use and land clearing |
| **Solar power technology** | Provided electricity to remote communities without damaging emissions, reducing reliance on fuel wood |
| **Improved medical technology** | Better diagnosis and treatment of diseases, extending and improving quality of life |
| **Motor vehicles and transport technology** | Faster movement of people and goods, but increased air pollution and traffic congestion in cities |

pages.title: Look at the picture
pages.body:
[[img:if65914e77|Fig 6.1  Science, technology, innovation, society and the environment as interconnected influences on one another]]

Notice that the connections between these four areas run in multiple directions, not just one. Society's needs can drive new scientific research, scientific discoveries can enable new technologies, technologies can spark further innovation, and all of these can, in turn, affect the environment, which then influences future scientific questions and societal priorities.

pages.title: Going further
pages.body:
> 💡 **Going further**

Understanding the relationship among science, technology, innovation and society helps citizens make informed decisions about new developments, rather than simply accepting or rejecting them without consideration. For example, weighing the clear benefits of improved transport technology against its environmental costs, such as air pollution, can help guide better choices, such as investing in cleaner vehicle technology or improved public transport systems.
